runtime_variants.name: Sun (sky)
runtime_variants.note: Renderer-owned sky geometry outside the world-object template table. The stored default uses two concentric discs. Later engines let theatre TWR X directives change angle, size and colour.

states.name: Sun with face (crew proximity)
states.note: Earlier ground-crew proximity handling changes the near sun model at the same time as the crew gesture. Middle and far pointers remain unchanged.

runtime_variants.name: Farm building (slalom source)
runtime_variants.note: FARM.INC replaces the saucer model when slalom=1. Authored octant lists retain their omitted roof faces. Destruction uses the ordinary fuel-dump wreck, not a tumbling saucer.

states.name: Destroyed
states.note: Slalom bmrtim calls gmdest: the farm becomes the shared fuel-dump wreck and emits twelve fragments. There is no separate collapsed-barn mesh.

runtime_variants.name: Tree (slalom source)
runtime_variants.note: Slalom replaces the shell with a tree. Its far template uses a line trunk. The separate foliage-only helper is also preserved below.

runtime_variants.name: Tree foliage only (unused source helper)
runtime_variants.note: Complete foliage-only tree model stored in the source; the selected slalom object template does not reference it.

runtime_variants.name: Tall Tet marker (slalom source)
runtime_variants.note: normaltet=0 adds a long stem. The course generator places two rows of six markers at different heights.

runtime_variants.name: Pond (slalom source; reused crater geometry)
runtime_variants.note: slalom=1 changes the crater span from 4,000 to 16,000 cm and fixes its colour to blue.

runtime_variants.name: Traffic aircraft (slalom source)
runtime_variants.note: Slalom replaces the saucer-launch site with an aircraft using the ordinary aircraft middle/far models. Three are placed at 1,310.72 m altitude; bmrstim follows their fixed attitude without launching enemies. Type 51 is not boardable.

note: Earlier-build geometry and additional code-referenced models; newer-build animation/colour routines are not assumed equivalent.

source_colours.note: Random and alternating colours advance once per DOS game frame; the viewer uses 30 preview frames per second. Timer-bit flashing uses the original PIT rate. Random output uses the original multiplicative generator with a fixed preview seed; gameplay consumes random numbers for many other purposes.
